title: The Brockian System
description: The Brockian phase-depth program end to end: a hidden five-fold structure on the number line, a depth-holonomy invariant that sees beyond residue-Fourier data and is provably complete, the D5 character layer, Bombieri-Vinogradov Layer 4 (Vaughan's identity), and the honest conditional frontier where famous conjectures reduce to named open hypotheses. Every verified result renders green; every conditional reduction renders as an explicit not-a-proof state.

claims.claim: Primes greater than 5 travel on fixed residue 'roads' mod 5: a cousin-prime pair (p, p+4) can only occupy the residue transitions (2->1), (3->2), or (4->3).
The residue walk of a fixed stride around the mod-5 cone is fully classified: every stride's ray sequence is determined.
The depth-holonomy invariant separates two transfer systems with identical residue-Fourier spectra: branching sees strictly beyond weighted-cyclic Fourier analysis.
No-go (invariance): on a single deterministic 5-cycle, cohomologous roofs share the same total depth - there is no additive invariant finer than the total.
Completeness (converse): equal total sum over the 5-cycle forces the difference to be a coboundary. With invariance, the total-depth invariant is COMPLETE - both directions proved.
The depth-holonomy group over a ZMod 6 fiber is an isomorphic copy of ZMod 6: the loop map is a faithful additive homomorphism onto the fiber translations.
Over a nonabelian S3 fiber the loop holonomy is order-dependent (the two seam elements do not commute) - the first non-order-independent holonomy in the program.
The five fifth-roots-of-unity additive characters on ZMod 5 satisfy Parseval's identity.
The additive characters are orthogonal: summing e(a*x) over ZMod 5 gives 5 when a=0 and 0 otherwise.
Vaughan's identity (Bombieri-Vinogradov Layer 4): the von Mangoldt function decomposes as a four-term Dirichlet-convolution identity for all truncation parameters U, V.
CONDITIONAL: the Twin Prime Conjecture follows from Dickson's conjecture on admissible k-tuples. The implication is proved; Dickson remains open.
CONDITIONAL: Brocard's problem (finitely many n with n!+1 a perfect square) follows from the ABC conjecture. The implication is proved; ABC remains open.
CONDITIONAL (equivalence): even-perfect-number infinitude is equivalent to Mersenne-exponent infinitude (Euclid-Euler). The equivalence is proved; neither open side is resolved.
